transcript.text: In this video, you’ll turn a sheet of letters into a font, then fine-tune it and make a colour version.
Open Fonts. The interface turns violet here, so you always know you’re working on letters.
Your fonts are listed on the left. Bubble Blue, Orange and Pearl come with the app.
Start with a sheet of letters in a grid, drawn by an AI image tool. This guide has prompts you can copy.
Choose the sheet, or drop it straight onto this window.
The app finds the grid, and removes the background around every letter.
It recognises which sheet this is, and names every cell in reading order: A, B, C, and so on.
Check the letters under the sheet. If a cell is wrong, type the right character into it.
Import into a new font, give it a name, and press Import.
Here’s your new font. Click any glyph to edit it.
Drag the letter to move it up or down, or drag the dotted line to change its spacing.
The exact numbers are right below: baseline, scale, and the space on each side.
Every change can be undone with Control Z.
Guides show the baseline, cap height, x-height, ascender and descender on every glyph. Turn on the ones you need.
Auto-place all sets every letter on the baseline for you, with the slight overshoot round letters need.
Even out sizes fixes sheets where each letter was stretched to fill its cell.
Type in the sample line to try your font on any words.
Colour variants recolour the whole font from its own artwork. No new sheets needed.
Pick a preset, or fine-tune the colours, then create the variant.
Give it a name, and press OK.
It appears in your list, ready to use in a title.
Save font file keeps a copy you can share, or open on another computer.
Export PSD sends every letter to Photoshop as its own layer. Update from PSD brings your edits back.
Next, let’s design a title with your font.
